mvgam_irf object description

Source: R/mvgam_irf-class.R
mvgam_irf-class.Rd

The objects returned by irf(). Run methods(class = "mvgam_irf") and methods(class = "mvgam_irf_summary") to see an overview of available methods.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam_irf'
summary(object, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), ...)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam_irf'
plot(x, series = 1, responses = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

An mvgam_irf object from irf(summary = FALSE).

probs

The lower and upper percentiles of the interval. Defaults to c(0.025, 0.975).

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

x

An mvgam_irf object.

series

Position or name of the process given the shock.

responses

Optional positions or names of the processes drawn as response panels. Defaults to every process.

Details

Generalized or Orthogonalized Impulse Response Functions are computed from the posterior estimates of Vector Autoregressive parameters. irf() applies a positive shock of one standard deviation to one process and calculates how each process in the latent VAR responds over h horizons, for every process in turn. Horizon 1 is the time step of the shock. stability() computes community-level metrics of stability from the same parameters.

A shock response is a K by K matrix per horizon per posterior draw. On a wide panel the draws run to hundreds of megabytes, where a median and an interval are what a reader uses. irf() returns the summary by default. The two forms carry different classes:

  • mvgam_irf_summary, the default. A long-format tibble inheriting from mvgam_var_surface_summary, with one row per shock-response pair per horizon. shock names the pair as "<from> -> <to>", taking the model's own series names where the latent processes are the series and "Process_k" where a factor VAR's processes are latent factors instead. horizon counts from 1, the time step of the shock. Three further columns hold the posterior median and the interval bounds, named for the percentiles asked for: irfQ50, irfQ2.5 and irfQ97.5 by default. An irf_type attribute records whether the responses are orthogonalised.

  • mvgam_irf, returned under summary = FALSE. A list with one element per posterior draw, each itself a list holding one h by K matrix of responses per shocked process. Pass it to summary() to reach the form above.

Both forms take ndraws and draw_ids. A subset of the posterior shortens the computation.

Methods

summary() turns the draws into the mvgam_irf_summary above, at the percentiles probs sets. plot() draws the response of each process to a shock to series, with its median and interval by horizon. A summary plots through plot.mvgam_var_surface_summary().

References

Pesaran HH and Shin Y (1998). Generalized impulse response analysis in linear multivariate models. Economics Letters 58, 17-29. doi:10.1016/S0165-1765(97)00214-0
